name: Quadratic assignment, QAPLIB sko56
description: Quadratic assignment problem, QAPLIB instance sko56: given two 56 x 56 integer matrices a and b, find a permutation p of 0..55 that minimises the cost, the sum over all i and j of a[i, j] * b[p[i], p[j]]. In the usual reading one matrix holds the flows between facilities and the other the distances between locations, and p assigns the one to the other; the cost formula is what is scored.
contract: solve(a, b) -> permutation p of 0..n-1 (a list of n integers, each exactly once). a and b are the first and second matrix of the QAPLIB file (int64 arrays of shape (n, n), passed as copies). Score: the exact integer cost, the sum over all i and j of a[i, j] * b[p[i], p[j]], minimized.
notes: sko56.dat from the QAPLIB deposit (Edinburgh DataShare, doi 10.7488/ds/3428, CC BY 4.0)
Skorin-Kapov instance with 56 facilities on a 7 x 8 rectangular grid: the distance matrix holds Manhattan distances between grid cells and the flow entries are pseudorandom integers.
Same evaluator contract as the existing QAPLIB tasks tai256c, tho150 and wil100 in autoresearch-tasks.
The record construction is public, so a candidate can embed the QAPLIB solution file; compare only genuinely searched results.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find a minimum-cost Koopmans-Beckmann quadratic assignment of 56 facilities to 56 locations for the QAPLIB instance sko56, which is not solved to optimality.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: The quadratic assignment problem models facility and hospital layout, keyboard design, backboard wiring and the generation of grey patterns. It is NP-hard and hard in practice: QAPLIB instances above about 30 facilities are mostly unsolved, and the best known solutions of the larger ones have stood for many years, so a cheaper permutation is a new best known solution of a standard open instance.
